_comment: CANONICAL contract for the Sentry PII scrub. tubermed-web/lib/sentry-scrub.ts and tubermed-backend/lib/sentry-scrub.js are two independent implementations of THIS document; each repo's own gate executes its implementation against it, and tubermed-backend/scripts/verify-mirror.js byte-compares its copy against this one. That composition is what makes 'the two scrubbers agree' a checked fact instead of a comment. Do NOT let an implementation read this file — an implementation that reads its own spec agrees with it by construction.
why: This is a medical product handling special-category data. An error payload must never carry a transcript, a request body, credentials, identity, or console context. sendDefaultPii:false prevents most of it; this contract makes it a guarantee.
_floor_warning: A refuter deleted entries from BOTH copies of this file and from the web implementation only: the copies stayed byte-identical, verify-mirror stayed green, and the web gate — which is contract-driven — weakened in lockstep with the spec it was checking. Each gate therefore carries its OWN hardcoded minimum set of channels, written in the gate source, and fails if this file drops below it. Mirroring proves the two specs are IDENTICAL; it can never prove either is STRONG.

url.why: On the browser SDK path query_string is never emitted at all — the query lives INSIDE request.url. What rides there: ?visit=<consultation uuid>, ?q=<free-text admin search>, and ?session=<sessionId>, which is the phone-upload credential.
url.policy_why: origin_and_pathname (v2) kept every path segment, and the same identifiers travel as path params: /api/sessions/:id IS the phone-upload credential, and thirteen /api/consultations/:id/... routes carry the note uuid. Origin-only would destroy route-level triage. route_shape keeps the route and loses the identifiers.

by_shape.hex_token: a segment of 8 or more characters, all of them [0-9a-f] case-insensitive — the phone session id is crypto.randomBytes(6).toString('hex'), always 12
by_shape.digits: a segment of one or more characters, all [0-9]

by_position.skip_empty_segments: A double slash used to defeat this rule outright: the segment after '//' saw an EMPTY previous segment, so nothing was a collection and nothing after it was an id. The previous NON-EMPTY segment is what counts.
by_position.why: Shape rules cannot catch a short or unusually-formed identifier, and the segment after a collection name IS an identifier by construction. A mistake here costs a route detail; a missing rule publishes a credential.

opaque_origin.why: For data:, blob:, file:, javascript: and mailto: URLs the parsed origin is the literal string 'null', and origin+pathname concatenated it onto an unstructured path — 'data:text/plain,PATIENT…' came out as 'nulltext/plain,PATIENT…', free text intact. Only http(s) URLs have a meaningful origin/pathname split, so anything else is replaced wholesale.

non_string.why: The reduction used to be gated on typeof url === 'string', so a String object or a {href} shape passed through untouched — a scrub-less failure direction.

message.redacted_to: [redacted: message not on the tag allowlist]

allow.pattern: ^\[account-status\] UNANSWERABLE — revocation NOT ENFORCED\. kind=[a-z_]+ unanswerable_total=\d+ checks_total=\d+$

message.pilot_leads_why: Added 2026-08-31, policy UNCHANGED (still v4, still full-string). The public lead form had captured zero leads since it shipped and the only place that failure was ever rendered was the visitor's own screen. Two call sites because the two silences are on opposite sides of the network: the backend one reports an insert the database refused; the browser one reports a request that got no answer at all (status=0), which is the ONLY witness available when a CORS preflight is refused and the POST is therefore never dispatched — no server-side channel can see a request the browser did not send. Both carry a status, a count, and nothing else; the payload of that form is a name and an e-mail address and never rides the event. `code` is normalised to [A-Z0-9_] at the call site before it reaches this pattern, because a PostgREST error object's `details`/`hint` echo the offending row.
message.why: captureMessage is called in production, so 'assert it empty' is not available — the assertion would be false on the first cap crossing. It is scrubbed instead.
message.policy_why: v3 matched a PREFIX, and a refuter rode arbitrary text in behind an allowed tag: '[usage-caps] пациент Иванов ЕГН …' survived verbatim. A prefix allowlist is the caller-discipline guarantee this contract exists to replace — the very argument used to drop breadcrumbs. Each allowed message now matches a FULL-STRING pattern that admits only counts and closed enums. drop_formatted is new for the same reason: logentry.formatted IS the interpolation of message+params, so dropping params while keeping formatted dropped the copy and kept the result.

tags.why: Tags are ours to set and nothing sets one today, so an empty allowlist costs nothing and stops the channel opening later. Adding a tag is a deliberate edit here, in both repos.

fingerprint.why: Nothing sets a fingerprint today. It can carry interpolated values if anyone ever does, so it is asserted empty and the assertion IS the guard — the argument that settled message.

transaction.why: KEPT, because it is the route name and carries the triage value that made keeping the path worth it. But on the browser SDK it is derived from location.pathname, so shipping it raw would restore the exact channel request.url just closed. It runs through the SAME segment rules.

known_residuals.unscrubbed_event_fields: Still neither deleted nor asserted: server_name, threads, spans, debug_meta. Nothing writes to them in either repo today. RULING OWED.
known_residuals.exception_value: exception.values[].value is keep-listed as verified non-PII (fixed literals / API strings). Measured, it passes arbitrary text through — that is discipline, not construction, and the backend attaches err.transcript to errors by design (non-enumerable, so the serializer does not reach it). RULING OWED.
known_residuals.encoded_query: A query encoded into the path (%3F) stays in pathname by definition, so it survives route_shape unless the encoded remainder happens to match a segment rule. Narrow: no code in either repo builds a URL that way.
known_residuals.below_floor_tokens: A 7-character hex, a ULID, a nanoid and a base64url token are not id-shaped by these rules and survive when they are NOT after a collection segment. No identifier this product mints has those shapes.

keep_why: The exception message and stack are what actually fix bugs. The method is a bare verb.
